_source.description: Major global lithium mining and production sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); S&P Global Market Intelligence; Albemarle, SQM, Pilbara Minerals, Ganfeng Lithium, Rio Tinto, Arcadium Lithium, Sigma Lithium, Liontown Resources, Core Lithium, ioneer, Eramet, Zijin Mining, Leo Lithium, AVZ Minerals, Atlantic Lithium, European Metals Holdings, Sibanye-Stillwater, Lepidico annual reports and ASX/SEC/TSX filings; Bolivia YLB/Comibol government publications
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary; Bolivia government data: public domain
_source.notes: Major lithium operations globally — operating mines, advanced development projects, and world-class deposits. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, NI 43-101/JORC technical reports, and satellite verification. Production/capacity figures from 2023 where available. All capacity figures in lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) tonnes per annum. Note: USGS reports lithium in Li metal content; figures here have been converted to LCE (multiply Li content by ~5.323). Australian hard-rock capacities converted from spodumene concentrate nameplate using standard ~6% Li2O recovery factors.

_coverage.global_production_source: USGS MCS 2024 — 180,000 t Li content × 5.323 = ~950,000 t LCE
_coverage.known_gaps: Smaller Chinese lepidolite operations in Jiangxi/Sichuan (~10-15% of global supply); emerging Argentine brine projects in Jujuy/Salta provinces; artisanal pegmatite mining in Zimbabwe and DRC

sites.name: Salar de Atacama
sites.notes: World's largest lithium brine operation; ~25% of global supply; combined SQM (~180k LCE) + Albemarle (~85k LCE) nameplate capacity

sites.name: Salar de Olaroz
sites.notes: Stage 2 expansion completed 2023, ramping to 42,500 tpa LCE

sites.name: Salar del Hombre Muerto
sites.notes: One of the longest-operating lithium brine operations in Argentina; Fenix expansion underway

sites.name: Cauchari-Olaroz
sites.ownership: Lithium Americas Argentina (44.8%), Ganfeng Lithium (46.7%), JEMSE (8.5%)
sites.notes: First production June 2023; ramping to 40,000 tpa LCE nameplate; adjacent to Salar de Olaroz

sites.name: Tres Quebradas
sites.ownership: Zijin Mining (100%, acquired from Neo Lithium 2022)
sites.notes: High-grade salar in Catamarca province; DFS completed; construction initiated by Zijin post-acquisition

sites.name: Sal de Vida
sites.notes: Adjacent to Salar del Hombre Muerto; Stage 1 (15,000 tpa) under construction, total 45,000 tpa planned

sites.name: Rincon
sites.ownership: Rio Tinto (100%, acquired Rincon Mining 2022 for $825M)
sites.notes: Salar de Rincon; Rio Tinto's flagship lithium project; starter plant under construction, full-scale 50,000 tpa planned

sites.name: Centenario-Ratones
sites.notes: Salta province; Eramet's DLE (direct lithium extraction) plant under construction; first production targeted 2024

sites.name: Maricunga
sites.notes: Blanco project on Salar de Maricunga; DFS completed; permitting in progress in Atacama region

sites.name: Pastos Grandes
sites.ownership: Bolivia state (Corporacion Minera de Bolivia / Yacimientos de Litio Bolivianos)
sites.notes: Secondary Bolivian salar under state-led exploration; pilot-scale DLE testing with CBC (China); 15,000 tpa LCE target for Comibol pilot plant

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni
sites.notes: World's largest lithium resource (~21 Mt Li); state-controlled; pilot plant operational; high Mg:Li ratio complicates extraction; DLE agreements with CATL/CBC and Russian Uranium One; 25,000 tpa LCE target for YLB industrial phase (operational challenges persist)

sites.name: Grota do Cirilo
sites.notes: Largest hard-rock lithium project in the Americas; Araçuaí/Itinga, Minas Gerais; first production April 2023; green (DMS) processing

sites.name: Greenbushes
sites.notes: World's largest hard-rock lithium mine; operating since 1983; Talison produces ~1.5M tpa spodumene concentrate (~200k LCE equivalent)

sites.name: Mt Cattlin
sites.notes: Open-pit spodumene mine near Ravensthorpe, WA

sites.name: Pilgangoora
sites.notes: Major Pilbara spodumene operation; P680 and P1000 expansion projects; ~680k tpa spodumene nameplate converts to ~90k LCE

sites.name: Wodgina
sites.ownership: Mineral Resources (50%), Albemarle (50%) via MARBL JV
sites.notes: Restarted in 2022 after care-and-maintenance; Train 1 & 2 operational; ~750k tpa spodumene nameplate converts to ~100k LCE

sites.name: Finniss
sites.notes: NT's first lithium mine; first shipment late 2022; operations suspended in early 2024 due to low spodumene prices

sites.name: Mt Holland
sites.notes: Earl Grey deposit; integrated mine-to-hydroxide project with refinery at Kwinana, WA; first production expected 2025

sites.name: Kathleen Valley
sites.notes: Major Tier-1 deposit near Leinster, WA; offtake agreements with Tesla and LG; commissioning 2024

sites.name: Bald Hill
sites.ownership: Alita Resources (formerly Tawana Resources; entered administration)
sites.notes: Mine placed on care-and-maintenance in 2019 after operator insolvency; high tantalum credits; near Norseman, WA

sites.name: Yichun (Jiangxi Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple operators including Ganfeng Lithium, Jiangxi Special Electric Motor
sites.notes: Yichun/Ningdu region hosts Asia's largest lepidolite reserves; multiple mines and processors

sites.name: Yajiang–Aba (Sichuan Province)
sites.notes: Lijiagou, Dangba, and surrounding spodumene deposits on the Tibetan Plateau margin

sites.name: Ningdu (Jiangxi Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple operators in Ningdu County pegmatite district
sites.notes: Southern Jiangxi lepidolite mining district; multiple small-to-medium mines; significant domestic supply source alongside Yichun cluster

sites.name: Dangxiongcuo (Tibet)
sites.notes: Tibetan Plateau salt lake lithium brine; exploration and pilot stage; extreme altitude (~4,500m) limits development; part of China's strategic lithium reserve base; 20,000 tpa LCE estimated target per Chinese government expansion plans

sites.name: Thacker Pass
sites.notes: Largest known lithium deposit in the US; Phase 1 construction underway in Humboldt County, NV

sites.name: Silver Peak
sites.notes: Only currently operating lithium mine in the US; Clayton Valley, NV; operating since 1966; small scale but strategically significant

sites.name: Kings Mountain (Carolina Lithium)
sites.notes: Historic Kings Mountain lithium belt, NC; Albemarle expansion project targeting 30,000 tpa LCE; previously operated by FMC/Livent until 1988

sites.name: Piedmont Lithium (Gaston County)
sites.notes: Carolina Tin-Spodumene Belt; PFS completed; local permitting challenges; offtake agreement with Tesla

sites.name: Rhyolite Ridge
sites.notes: Unique lithium-boron deposit in Esmeralda County, NV; DOE conditional loan commitment of $700M; first production targeted 2026

sites.name: Whabouchi
sites.notes: One of Canada's largest lithium deposits; in development with Becancour hydroxide plant

sites.name: James Bay
sites.notes: Large open-pit spodumene deposit in northern Quebec; DFS completed; construction decision pending; near Cree Nation of Eastmain territory

sites.name: Rose Lithium-Tantalum
sites.notes: Eeyou Istchee James Bay, Quebec; FS completed 2023; significant tantalum by-product credits

sites.name: Goulamina
sites.ownership: Ganfeng Lithium (majority, via JV with Leo Lithium); Mali state (10% carried interest)
sites.notes: One of the largest undeveloped spodumene deposits globally; southern Mali near Bougouni; DFS completed; Ganfeng controlling operations post-restructuring

sites.name: Arcadia
sites.ownership: Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt (majority, acquired from Prospect Resources 2022)
sites.notes: Near Harare; one of Africa's largest lithium deposits; fast-tracked to production under Chinese ownership; open-pit petalite and spodumene

sites.name: Bikita
sites.notes: Historic mine operating since 1950s; Masvingo Province; one of the oldest lithium mines globally; expanded under Sinomine ownership

sites.name: Karibib (Rubicon/Desert Lion)
sites.notes: Karibib pegmatite field, Erongo Region; Lepidico's L-Max processing technology; small-scale development project

sites.name: Manono
sites.ownership: AVZ Minerals (75% in Dathcom Mining JV, under dispute); Cominiere (25%)
sites.notes: One of world's largest hard-rock lithium deposits (400 Mt at 1.65%); Tanganyika Province; ownership dispute ongoing with CATH/Zijin interests

sites.name: Ewoyaa
sites.ownership: Atlantic Lithium (majority); Piedmont Lithium (offtake partner); Ghana government (13% carried interest)
sites.notes: Cape Coast area, Central Region; DFS completed; potentially first lithium mine in West Africa; mining license granted 2024

sites.name: Jadar
sites.notes: Unique jadarite mineral deposit discovered 2004; permits reinstated by Serbian court 2024 after earlier government revocation

sites.name: Cinovec
sites.ownership: European Metals Holdings (49% via Geomet JV); CEZ Group (51%)
sites.notes: Largest lithium deposit in Europe; Krusne Hory/Erzgebirge (Ore Mountains) on Czech-German border; underground mine planned; PFS completed

sites.name: Wolfsberg
sites.notes: Koralpe region, Carinthia; one of few European spodumene deposits; DFS completed; JORC resource defined; underground mine planned

sites.name: Keliber (Kaustinen)
sites.notes: Ostrobothnia region; integrated mine-to-hydroxide project; multiple pegmatite deposits; Kokkola chemical plant; construction underway

sites.name: San Jose (Caceres)
sites.ownership: Infinity Lithium (75%), Extremadura New Energies JV
sites.notes: San Jose deposit near Caceres, Extremadura; underground mine planned; close to historic tin workings; environmental opposition from city

sites.name: Emili (Barroso)
sites.notes: Barroso region, northern Portugal (Boticas); JORC resource defined; EIA submitted; local opposition from agricultural/environmental groups; could become first Portuguese lithium mine
